paragraphs.title: Gathering the Assembly and Preparing the Ordination Ceremony

easy.question: Who spoke to Moses at the beginning of the passage?
answers: The Lord
Aaron
The whole assembly
easy.explanation: The first verse says, “The Lord spoke to Moses.”

easy.question: Whom did the Lord command Moses to take, along with the garments and anointing oil?
answers: The whole assembly
Aaron and his sons
The priests only
easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, “Take Aaron and his sons with him.”

easy.question: Where was the whole assembly gathered?
answers: The Israelite camp
The altar
The door of the tabernacle
easy.explanation: The assembly was gathered at the door of the tabernacle.

medium.question: What did Moses do after the Lord commanded him to gather the assembly?
answers: He did as the Lord commanded
He sent Aaron alone
He waited for the people to come by themselves
medium.explanation: Moses obeyed the command, and the assembly gathered at the tabernacle.

medium.question: In the phrase “Gather all the assembly together to the door of the tabernacle,” what does “gather” mean?
answers: Scatter
Bring together
Bless
medium.explanation: “Gather” means to bring people together in one place.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: The assembly gathered, then the Lord commanded Moses
Moses spoke to the assembly, then the Lord spoke to him
The Lord commanded Moses, Moses obeyed, and the assembly gathered
medium.explanation: First came the command, then Moses obeyed, and then the assembly gathered.

challenge.question: Which list correctly describes what Moses was commanded to bring?
answers: A bull for a sin offering, two rams, and a basket of unleavened bread
Two bulls, one ram, and a basket of fruit
One lamb, two grain offerings, and silver vessels
challenge.explanation: Verse 2 lists a bull for the sin offering, two rams, and a basket of unleavened bread, along with Aaron, his sons, the garments, and the oil.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the assembly being gathered before Moses said, “This is the thing”?
answers: The assembly was meant to be present and hear the command
The assembly had to choose the priests
The assembly had already performed the ceremony
challenge.explanation: The people gathered at the tabernacle entrance, where Moses announced what the Lord had commanded.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “as the Lord commanded him” emphasize about Moses?
answers: He changed the command according to his own opinion
He acted exactly according to the command
He did not understand the command
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes Moses’ exact obedience to the Lord.

questions.question: Which list correctly describes what Moses was commanded to bring?
answers: A bull for a sin offering, two rams, and a basket of unleavened bread
Two bulls, one ram, and a basket of fruit
One lamb, two grain offerings, and silver vessels
questions.explanation: Verse 2 lists a bull for the sin offering, two rams, and a basket of unleavened bread.

questions.question: What can we infer from the assembly being gathered before Moses said, “This is the thing”?
answers: The assembly was meant to be present and hear the command
The assembly had to choose the priests
The assembly had already performed the ceremony
questions.explanation: The people gathered at the tabernacle entrance to hear what the Lord had commanded.

questions.question: What does the phrase “as the Lord commanded him” emphasize about Moses?
answers: He changed the command according to his own opinion
He acted exactly according to the command
He did not understand the command
questions.explanation: It emphasizes that Moses carried out the Lord’s command exactly.

paragraphs.title: Washing Aaron and Dressing the High Priest

easy.question: Whom did Moses bring and wash with water?
answers: Aaron and his sons
The priests only
The Israelites
easy.explanation: Moses brought Aaron and his sons and washed them with water.

easy.question: With what did Moses wash Aaron and his sons?
answers: Oil
Water
Blood
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says that he washed them with water.

easy.question: What did Moses place on Aaron’s head at the end of the description?
answers: The ephod
The breastplate
The turban
easy.explanation: Verse 9 says Moses placed the turban on Aaron’s head.

medium.question: What did Moses do after washing Aaron and his sons?
answers: He dressed Aaron in the priestly garments
He offered a sacrifice
He anointed them with oil
medium.explanation: After washing them, Moses dressed Aaron in the priestly garments.

medium.question: In the phrase “He girded him with the sash,” what is a sash?
answers: A hat
A belt or band
A sacred vessel
medium.explanation: A sash is a belt or band worn around the body.

medium.question: What is the correct order according to the verses?
answers: The turban, washing, the ephod, the breastplate
The breastplate, washing, the turban, the robe
Washing, the priestly garments, the breastplate, the turban and holy crown
medium.explanation: First came the washing, then the garments, followed by the breastplate, turban, and holy crown.

challenge.question: What special detail is given about the holy crown in relation to the turban?
answers: It was placed under the turban
It was placed on the turban at the front
It was tied around Aaron’s waist
challenge.explanation: The crown was placed on the front of the turban.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the move from dressing Aaron to placing the breastplate and crown?
answers: The preparation took place in ordered stages
The breastplate and crown were not priestly garments
Aaron dressed himself
challenge.explanation: The sequence shows that Aaron’s preparation was completed step by step.

challenge.question: What do the words “as the Lord commanded Moses” emphasize?
answers: The act was done only after the people requested it
Moses chose the clothing himself
The actions were carried out according to God’s command
challenge.explanation: The ending emphasizes that Moses dressed Aaron as he had been commanded.

questions.question: What special detail is given about the holy crown in relation to the turban?
answers: It was placed under the turban
It was placed on the turban at the front
It was tied around Aaron’s waist
questions.explanation: The crown was placed on the front of the turban.

questions.question: What can we infer from the move from dressing Aaron to placing the breastplate and crown?
answers: The preparation took place in ordered stages
The breastplate and crown were not priestly garments
Aaron dressed himself
questions.explanation: The sequence shows that Aaron’s preparation was completed step by step.

questions.question: What do the words “as the Lord commanded Moses” emphasize?
answers: The act was done only after the people requested it
Moses chose the clothing himself
The actions were carried out according to God’s command
questions.explanation: The ending emphasizes that Moses dressed Aaron as he had been commanded.

paragraphs.title: Consecrating the Tabernacle, the Altar, and Aaron

easy.question: What did Moses take in order to anoint the tabernacle?
answers: Anointing oil
Water
Blood
easy.explanation: The verse says that Moses took the anointing oil.

easy.question: Whom did Moses anoint with the anointing oil at the end of the passage?
answers: Aaron
Eleazar
The Israelites
easy.explanation: Moses poured the oil on Aaron’s head and anointed him.

easy.question: How many times did Moses sprinkle the oil on the altar?
answers: Three times
Seven times
Ten times
easy.explanation: Verse 11 says that he sprinkled it on the altar seven times.

medium.question: What was the purpose of the anointing and sprinkling?
answers: To consecrate them
To clean them
To hide them
medium.explanation: The actions were performed to consecrate the tabernacle, its vessels, the altar, and Aaron.

medium.question: In the phrase “He sprinkled some of it on the altar,” what does “sprinkled” mean?
answers: Poured all of it
Scattered or splashed some of it
Hid it
medium.explanation: The wording indicates that some oil was scattered or splashed on the altar, seven times.

medium.question: What was done first?
answers: Aaron was anointed
Oil was sprinkled on the altar
The tabernacle and everything in it were anointed
medium.explanation: Moses first anointed the tabernacle and everything in it, then the altar, and finally Aaron.

challenge.question: What special detail is given about the sprinkling, unlike the other anointings?
answers: It was done seven times
It was done on Aaron’s head
It was done only inside the tabernacle
challenge.explanation: Only the sprinkling on the altar is specifically said to have been done seven times.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Moses anointing both the vessels and Aaron?
answers: Only Aaron was considered holy
Consecration involved both the place of worship and the person serving there
The vessels replaced Aaron
challenge.explanation: The verses connect the consecration of the tabernacle and its vessels with the consecration of Aaron.

challenge.question: What wording distinguishes Moses’ action toward Aaron from his action toward the altar?
answers: Oil was poured on Aaron and sprinkled on the altar
Aaron was consecrated and the altar was poured
Aaron was sprinkled and the altar was anointed
challenge.explanation: The oil was poured on Aaron’s head, while it was sprinkled on the altar.

questions.question: What special detail is given about the sprinkling, unlike the other anointings?
answers: It was done seven times
It was done on Aaron’s head
It was done only inside the tabernacle
questions.explanation: Only the sprinkling on the altar is specifically said to have been done seven times.

questions.question: What can we infer from Moses anointing both the vessels and Aaron?
answers: Only Aaron was considered holy
Consecration involved both the place of worship and the person serving there
The vessels replaced Aaron
questions.explanation: The verses connect the consecration of the tabernacle and its vessels with the consecration of Aaron.

questions.question: What wording distinguishes Moses’ action toward Aaron from his action toward the altar?
answers: Oil was poured on Aaron and sprinkled on the altar
Aaron was consecrated and the altar was poured
Aaron was sprinkled and the altar was anointed
questions.explanation: The oil was poured on Aaron’s head, while it was sprinkled on the altar.

paragraphs.title: Dressing Aaron’s Sons and Offering the Sin Offering

easy.question: What did Moses put on Aaron’s sons?
answers: Tunics, sashes, and caps
Robes and shoes
Crowns and cloaks
easy.explanation: Moses put tunics on them, girded them with sashes, and put caps on them.

easy.question: Who laid their hands on the head of the sin-offering bull?
answers: Moses alone
Aaron and his sons
All the Israelites
easy.explanation: Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the bull’s head.

easy.question: Where were the bull, its hide, flesh, and dung burned?
answers: On the altar
Inside the tabernacle
Outside the camp
easy.explanation: The bull and its remaining parts were burned outside the camp.

medium.question: What happened after Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the bull?
answers: The bull was slaughtered
The bull was returned to the herd
The bull was taken outside the camp
medium.explanation: Moses slaughtered the sin-offering bull after they laid their hands on it.

medium.question: In the phrase “He put caps on them,” what are caps?
answers: Belts
Head coverings
Sacred vessels
medium.explanation: Because they were placed on their heads, the caps were head coverings.

medium.question: Why did Moses put some blood on the altar and pour the rest at its base?
answers: To decorate the altar
To moisten the fire
To purify, consecrate, and make atonement for the altar
medium.explanation: The blood was used to purify and consecrate the altar and make atonement for it.

challenge.question: Which sequence correctly describes what Moses did with the bull’s blood?
answers: Put it on the altar’s horns, poured the rest at its base, and purified the altar
Poured it at the base, burned it, and ate it
Put it on the priests’ garments, poured it on the bull, and purified the camp
challenge.explanation: Moses put the blood on the altar’s horns, poured the remainder at its base, and thereby purified and consecrated it.

challenge.question: What was offered on the altar, and what was burned outside the camp?
answers: The hide on the altar and the fat outside the camp
The fat and inner parts on the altar, and the rest of the bull outside the camp
The entire bull on the altar, with nothing outside the camp
challenge.explanation: The fat and inner parts were burned on the altar; the bull and its remaining parts were burned outside the camp.

challenge.question: What does the repeated phrase “as the Lord commanded Moses” teach?
answers: The actions followed God’s command
Moses acted only on his own idea
The ceremony had no fixed order
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that Moses carried out the instructions according to the Lord’s command.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes what Moses did with the bull’s blood?
answers: Put it on the altar’s horns, poured the rest at its base, and purified the altar
Poured it at the base, burned it, and ate it
Put it on the priests’ garments, poured it on the bull, and purified the camp
questions.explanation: Moses put the blood on the altar’s horns, poured the remainder at its base, and purified the altar.

questions.question: What was offered on the altar, and what was burned outside the camp?
answers: The hide on the altar and the fat outside the camp
The fat and inner parts on the altar, and the rest of the bull outside the camp
The entire bull on the altar, with nothing outside the camp
questions.explanation: The fat and inner parts were burned on the altar; the remaining bull was burned outside the camp.

questions.question: What does the repeated phrase “as the Lord commanded Moses” teach?
answers: The actions followed God’s command
Moses acted only on his own idea
The ceremony had no fixed order
questions.explanation: It emphasizes that Moses carried out the instructions according to the Lord’s command.

paragraphs.title: Offering the Ram for the Burnt Offering

easy.question: Who laid their hands on the ram’s head?
answers: Aaron and his sons
Moses
The Israelites
easy.explanation: Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.

easy.question: What did Moses do with the ram’s blood?
answers: Washed it with water
Sprinkled it around the altar
Poured it outside the camp
easy.explanation: Moses sprinkled the blood around the altar.

easy.question: What was offered on the altar at the end of the process?
answers: Only the ram’s head
Only the blood
The whole ram
easy.explanation: Moses burned the whole ram on the altar.

medium.question: What happened to the ram after Aaron and his sons laid their hands on it?
answers: It was slaughtered
It was washed with water
It was returned to the flock
medium.explanation: The next step was the slaughtering of the ram.

medium.question: Why were the inner parts and legs washed with water before the offering?
answers: To prepare them for eating
To prepare them for burning on the altar
To return them to the ram
medium.explanation: The washing prepared these parts for the offering on the altar.

medium.question: In the phrase “the head, the pieces, and the fat,” what does “fat” refer to?
answers: The animal’s sacrificial fat
The animal’s blood
The animal’s hide
medium.explanation: The fat is listed with the parts of the ram burned on the altar.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the statement that Moses burned “the whole ram”?
answers: The entire ram was to be burned on the altar
Only the blood was offered
Aaron and his sons ate the ram
challenge.explanation: “The whole ram” emphasizes that it was not only selected parts that were offered.

challenge.question: Which sequence matches the verses?
answers: Washing, laying on hands, slaughtering, burning
Laying on hands, slaughtering, sprinkling the blood, burning
Burning, sprinkling the blood, laying on hands, washing
challenge.explanation: First they laid hands on the ram, then it was slaughtered, its blood was sprinkled, and its parts were burned.

challenge.question: What does the word “around” emphasize in the description of the blood?
answers: The blood was sprinkled around the altar
The blood was sprinkled only inside the ram
The blood was poured far from the altar
challenge.explanation: “Around” describes the blood being applied around the altar rather than in one place.

questions.question: What can we infer from the statement that Moses burned “the whole ram”?
answers: The entire ram was to be burned on the altar
Only the blood was offered
Aaron and his sons ate the ram
questions.explanation: “The whole ram” emphasizes that the entire animal was offered.

questions.question: Which sequence matches the verses?
answers: Washing, laying on hands, slaughtering, burning
Laying on hands, slaughtering, sprinkling the blood, burning
Burning, sprinkling the blood, laying on hands, washing
questions.explanation: First they laid hands on the ram, then it was slaughtered, its blood was sprinkled, and it was burned.

questions.question: What does the word “around” emphasize in the description of the blood?
answers: The blood was sprinkled around the altar
The blood was sprinkled only inside the ram
The blood was poured far from the altar
questions.explanation: It describes the blood being applied around the altar.

paragraphs.title: The Ram of Consecration and the Consecrating Blood

easy.question: Who laid their hands on the head of the second ram?
answers: Aaron and his sons
Moses and his sons
The Israelites
easy.explanation: Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.

easy.question: On which parts of Aaron did Moses put some of the blood?
answers: His head and shoulders
The tip of his ear, the thumb of his hand, and the big toe of his right foot
Both hands and both feet
easy.explanation: The blood was put on Aaron’s right ear, right thumb, and right big toe.

easy.question: What did Moses do with the blood that remained?
answers: Poured it outside the camp
Put it on the priests’ garments
Sprinkled it around the altar
easy.explanation: Moses sprinkled the remaining blood around the altar.

medium.question: What is the order of events in the verses?
answers: The ram was brought, hands were laid on it, it was slaughtered, and blood was applied
It was slaughtered, blood was sprinkled, hands were laid on it, and it was offered
Blood was applied, the ram was offered, blood was sprinkled, and it was slaughtered
medium.explanation: The ram was brought and presented, hands were laid on it, it was slaughtered, and Moses applied its blood.

medium.question: In the phrase “the thumb of his right hand,” what is a thumb?
answers: The large finger
The whole palm
The elbow
medium.explanation: A thumb is the large, opposing finger of the hand.

medium.question: Why does the passage repeatedly mention the right ear, hand, and foot?
answers: Only the right side was part of the body
The ceremony specifically involved the right side
Moses could not reach the left side
medium.explanation: The repeated reference to the right side is a deliberate detail of the ceremony.

challenge.question: What can we infer from blood being placed on the ear, hand, and foot?
answers: The ceremony involved hearing, actions, and the way the priests walked
The priests were wounded in three places
The blood was only for physical cleaning
challenge.explanation: The ear, hand, and foot can represent the consecration of hearing, actions, and conduct.

challenge.question: What distinguishes the treatment of the ram’s blood from the final step?
answers: First blood was placed on specific body parts, and finally it was sprinkled on the altar
First it was sprinkled on the altar, and finally it was put on the ears
Blood was put on Aaron but not on his sons
challenge.explanation: Blood was first applied to Aaron and his sons, and then the remainder was sprinkled around the altar.

challenge.question: What can we learn from Moses bringing Aaron’s sons after acting on Aaron?
answers: Only Aaron was connected with the ceremony
The same action was done first for Aaron and then for his sons
Aaron’s sons served in place of the ram
challenge.explanation: The passage describes the action first for Aaron and then for his sons in parallel detail.

questions.question: What can we infer from blood being placed on the ear, hand, and foot?
answers: The ceremony involved hearing, actions, and the way the priests walked
The priests were wounded in three places
The blood was only for physical cleaning
questions.explanation: The ear, hand, and foot can represent the consecration of hearing, actions, and conduct.

questions.question: What distinguishes the treatment of the ram’s blood from the final step?
answers: First blood was placed on specific body parts, and finally it was sprinkled on the altar
First it was sprinkled on the altar, and finally it was put on the ears
Blood was put on Aaron but not on his sons
questions.explanation: Blood was first applied to Aaron and his sons, and then the remainder was sprinkled around the altar.

questions.question: What can we learn from Moses bringing Aaron’s sons after acting on Aaron?
answers: Only Aaron was connected with the ceremony
The same action was done first for Aaron and then for his sons
Aaron’s sons served in place of the ram
questions.explanation: The passage describes the same action first for Aaron and then for his sons.

paragraphs.title: The Wave Offering and the Consecration Offering

easy.question: Which parts did Moses take from the ram?
answers: The fat, the kidneys, and the right thigh
Only the breast
Only the head
easy.explanation: Moses took the fat, the kidneys and their fat, and the right thigh.

easy.question: On whose hands were all these things placed?
answers: Moses’ hands
Aaron’s and his sons’ hands
The Israelites’ hands
easy.explanation: Everything was placed on Aaron’s hands and his sons’ hands.

easy.question: To whom did the breast belong as a portion?
answers: Aaron
Aaron’s sons
Moses
easy.explanation: The breast was Moses’ portion.

medium.question: What did Aaron and his sons do after everything was placed on their hands?
answers: They waved it before the Lord
They ate it immediately
They returned it to the basket
medium.explanation: They waved the items before the Lord as a wave offering.

medium.question: In the phrase “one wafer,” what is a wafer?
answers: A piece of meat
A thin, flat cake
A container for oil
medium.explanation: A wafer is a thin, flat cake; here it was part of the unleavened bread.

medium.question: What happened after Moses took the items from Aaron’s and his sons’ hands?
answers: He gave them to the people
He returned them to the basket
He burned them on the altar
medium.explanation: Moses burned them on the altar, on top of the burnt offering.

challenge.question: What does the repeated phrase “before the Lord” show?
answers: The actions were part of a ceremony performed before the Lord
The people stood outside the camp
The objects were hidden from the people
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the waving and consecration were acts of worship before the Lord.

challenge.question: What does “as the Lord commanded Moses” emphasize?
answers: The ceremony was performed quickly
Moses acted according to the Lord’s command
The breast belonged to all the people
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that Moses carried out the ceremony as commanded.

challenge.question: What was the difference between the breast and the other items taken from the ram?
answers: The breast was not waved
The breast was dedicated to Aaron and the rest was given to the people
The breast was waved and given to Moses, while the other items were burned on the altar
challenge.explanation: The other items were burned, while the breast was waved and became Moses’ portion.

questions.question: What does the repeated phrase “before the Lord” show?
answers: The actions were part of a ceremony performed before the Lord
The people stood outside the camp
The objects were hidden from the people
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the actions were part of worship before the Lord.

questions.question: What does “as the Lord commanded Moses” emphasize?
answers: The ceremony was performed quickly
Moses acted according to the Lord’s command
The breast belonged to all the people
questions.explanation: It emphasizes that Moses carried out the ceremony as commanded.

questions.question: What was the difference between the breast and the other items taken from the ram?
answers: The breast was not waved
The breast was dedicated to Aaron and the rest was given to the people
The breast was waved and given to Moses, while the other items were burned on the altar
questions.explanation: The other items were burned, while the breast was waved and became Moses’ portion.

paragraphs.title: Sprinkling Oil and Blood on the Priests

easy.question: What did Moses take in order to sprinkle?
answers: Anointing oil and blood from the altar
Water and incense
Bread and wine
easy.explanation: Moses took anointing oil and blood from the altar.

easy.question: On whom did Moses sprinkle them?
answers: The Israelites only
Aaron, his sons, and their garments
The altar only
easy.explanation: He sprinkled Aaron, his garments, his sons, and their garments.

easy.question: Whom did Moses consecrate?
answers: Aaron alone
Aaron’s sons alone
Aaron, his sons, and their garments
easy.explanation: The verse says that Moses consecrated Aaron, his sons, and their garments.

medium.question: What was the order of Moses’ actions?
answers: He took oil and blood, sprinkled them, and then consecrated
He consecrated, sprinkled, and then took oil and blood
He sprinkled, took oil and blood, and then consecrated
medium.explanation: First Moses took the oil and blood, then sprinkled them, and finally consecrated the priests and garments.

medium.question: In the phrase “he sprinkled it upon Aaron,” what does “sprinkled” mean?
answers: Hid
Scattered or splashed drops
Called out
medium.explanation: Here it means that Moses scattered or splashed drops of the oil and blood.

medium.question: What did Aaron and his sons have in common in this verse?
answers: They both took the oil and blood
They were both on the altar
Moses sprinkled and consecrated both them and their garments
medium.explanation: Moses sprinkled and consecrated both Aaron and his sons, along with their garments.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the repeated words “Aaron … his garments … his sons … their garments”?
answers: The consecration included both the people and their garments
Only the garments were consecrated
The sons were not involved
challenge.explanation: The detailed wording emphasizes that both the priests and their garments were included.

challenge.question: In the phrase “his sons and their garments with him,” what does “with him” include?
answers: The blood on the altar
The sons and their garments together
The anointing oil only
challenge.explanation: The phrase joins the sons and their garments as participants in the same action.

challenge.question: What does the use of both anointing oil and altar blood emphasize?
answers: Only one substance was used
The blood came from the sons’ garments
The action involved two different substances
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly names two substances: anointing oil and blood from the altar.

questions.question: What can we infer from the repeated words “Aaron … his garments … his sons … their garments”?
answers: The consecration included both the people and their garments
Only the garments were consecrated
The sons were not involved
questions.explanation: The wording emphasizes that both the priests and their garments were included.

questions.question: In the phrase “his sons and their garments with him,” what does “with him” include?
answers: The blood on the altar
The sons and their garments together
The anointing oil only
questions.explanation: It joins the sons and their garments as participants in the same action.

questions.question: What does the use of both anointing oil and altar blood emphasize?
answers: Only one substance was used
The blood came from the sons’ garments
The action involved two different substances
questions.explanation: The verse names anointing oil and blood from the altar as the two substances used.

paragraphs.title: Eating the Meat and Bread in the Holy Place

easy.question: To whom did Moses give the instructions in the verse?
answers: Aaron and his sons
All Israel
The elders of the people
easy.explanation: Moses spoke to Aaron and his sons.

easy.question: Where were Aaron and his sons to eat the meat?
answers: Inside the camp
At the door of the tabernacle
In their homes
easy.explanation: They were commanded to boil and eat it at the door of the tabernacle.

easy.question: What else were Aaron and his sons told to eat besides the meat?
answers: Fruit
Manna
The bread in the basket of consecration
easy.explanation: They were also to eat the bread in the basket of consecration.

medium.question: What does the phrase “as I commanded” mean in the verse?
answers: The instructions were to be followed
The order of eating could be changed
The bread did not need to be eaten
medium.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that Aaron and his sons were to follow Moses’ instructions.

medium.question: In the phrase “the basket of consecration,” what does “consecration” refer to?
answers: A basket filled with water
The dedication or initiation of the priests for their service
Collecting food for the whole people
medium.explanation: The basket was connected with the ceremony dedicating and initiating the priests.

medium.question: What order of actions is described?
answers: Eat bread, boil meat, then leave
Boil the meat, leave the tabernacle, then eat
Boil the meat and eat it with the bread at the appointed place
medium.explanation: They were first to boil the meat and then eat it with the bread at the tabernacle entrance.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the emphasis that “Aaron and his sons shall eat it”?
answers: Eating was part of their special priestly role
All Israel had to eat the meat
The meat was intended only for Moses
challenge.explanation: The emphasis shows that the food was connected with Aaron and his sons’ priestly service and initiation.

challenge.question: Which exact location is given for eating?
answers: Inside the tabernacle
At the door of the tabernacle
Outside the camp
challenge.explanation: The verse specifically says “at the door of the tabernacle.”

challenge.question: Why are the meat and the bread mentioned together?
answers: To teach that the bread replaced the meat
To say that only the bread was eaten
To show that both were part of the ritual meal the priests were commanded to eat
challenge.explanation: The verse gives one instruction concerning both the meat and the bread.

questions.question: What can we infer from the emphasis that “Aaron and his sons shall eat it”?
answers: Eating was part of their special priestly role
All Israel had to eat the meat
The meat was intended only for Moses
questions.explanation: The food was connected with Aaron and his sons’ priestly service and initiation.

questions.question: Which exact location is given for eating?
answers: Inside the tabernacle
At the door of the tabernacle
Outside the camp
questions.explanation: The verse specifically says “at the door of the tabernacle.”

questions.question: Why are the meat and the bread mentioned together?
answers: To teach that the bread replaced the meat
To say that only the bread was eaten
To show that both were part of the ritual meal the priests were commanded to eat
questions.explanation: Both the meat and bread were part of the ritual meal.

easy.question: What was to be done with the meat that remained?
answers: It was to be burned in the fire
It was to be eaten immediately
It was to be saved for the next day
easy.explanation: The verse commands that the remaining meat be burned with fire.

easy.question: What else is mentioned besides the meat?
answers: Water
Bread
Oil
easy.explanation: The verse also mentions the bread.

easy.question: By what means was the remainder to be burned?
answers: With water
In the sun
With fire
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “You shall burn it with fire.”

medium.question: What was to be done when meat or bread remained?
answers: They were to be burned with fire
They were to be distributed to people
They were to be returned to their place
medium.explanation: The command to burn applies to whatever remained of the meat and bread.

medium.question: In the phrase “what remains of the meat and bread,” what does “remains” mean?
answers: Disappears
Is left over
Is new
medium.explanation: “Remains” means what is left over.

medium.question: To which two things did the command to burn apply?
answers: The meat only
The bread only
Both the meat and the bread
medium.explanation: The verse mentions both meat and bread and commands that whatever remained be burned.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the command to burn what remained?
answers: The meat and bread were not to be saved for later use
Everything had to be eaten immediately
Fire was forbidden
challenge.explanation: Burning the remainder prevented it from being kept for later use.

challenge.question: Which wording shows that the command applies to two kinds of food?
answers: The word “fire”
The phrase “and of the bread” after “of the meat”
The word “burn” alone
challenge.explanation: The added phrase “and of the bread” includes bread along with meat.

challenge.question: If both meat and bread remained, what common rule applied to both?
answers: Save both
Eat both
Burn both with fire
challenge.explanation: The command to burn the remainder applies to both kinds of food.

answers: The meat and bread were not to be saved for later use
Everything had to be eaten immediately
Fire was forbidden
questions.explanation: Burning the remainder prevented it from being kept for later use.

questions.question: Which wording shows that the command applies to two kinds of food?
answers: The word “fire”
The phrase “and of the bread” after “of the meat”
The word “burn” alone
questions.explanation: The phrase “and of the bread” includes bread along with meat.

questions.question: If both meat and bread remained, what common rule applied to both?
answers: Save both
Eat both
Burn both with fire
questions.explanation: The command to burn the remainder applies to both kinds of food.

paragraphs.title: The Seven Days of Consecration and the Charge to Keep

easy.question: How many days were the priests to remain at the door of the tabernacle?
answers: Seven days
Three days
One day
easy.explanation: The verses repeatedly state that they were to remain there seven days.

easy.question: Where were the priests commanded to stay?
answers: Outside the camp
At the door of the tabernacle
Inside the city
easy.explanation: They were told to remain at the door of the tabernacle.

easy.question: What could happen if the priests did not keep the Lord’s command?
answers: They would have to begin again
They would lose their garments
They could die
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Keep the charge of the Lord, that you die not.”

medium.question: Why did the priests have to remain at the tabernacle for seven days?
answers: To study the Torah
To keep the Lord’s command and complete their consecration
To wait for the Israelites
medium.explanation: Their stay fulfilled the command and completed the period of their consecration.

medium.question: Which description applies to all seven days?
answers: The priests left during the day and returned at night
The priests served only in the morning
The priests remained there day and night and kept the Lord’s command
medium.explanation: They were to remain there day and night for seven days and keep the Lord’s charge.

medium.question: In the phrase “keep the charge of the Lord,” what does “charge” mean?
answers: A duty or responsibility to be kept
A place to live
A special garment
medium.explanation: Here “charge” means a duty or responsibility that must be faithfully observed.

challenge.question: How do the commands “You shall not go out” and “At the door of the tabernacle you shall remain” fit together?
answers: The priests could leave only at night
Both commands require them to remain near the entrance and not leave
The first command was for the people and the second for the priests
challenge.explanation: Both statements describe the priests remaining at the tabernacle entrance for seven days.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the phrase “until the days of your consecration are at an end”?
answers: The ceremony ended that same day
The priests waited for more people to arrive
The priests had to complete a defined period of consecration
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to completing the appointed period of the priests’ consecration.

challenge.question: What does Moses add by saying, “for so I am commanded”?
answers: His instructions came from the command he had received
The priests invented the command themselves
The command applied to only one day
challenge.explanation: Moses explains that these instructions were not his personal decision but a command he had received.

questions.question: How do the commands “You shall not go out” and “At the door of the tabernacle you shall remain” fit together?
answers: The priests could leave only at night
Both commands require them to remain near the entrance and not leave
The first command was for the people and the second for the priests
questions.explanation: Both commands require the priests to remain at the tabernacle entrance for seven days.

questions.question: What can we understand from the phrase “until the days of your consecration are at an end”?
answers: The ceremony ended that same day
The priests waited for more people to arrive
The priests had to complete a defined period of consecration
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to completing the appointed period of consecration.

questions.question: What does Moses add by saying, “for so I am commanded”?
answers: His instructions came from the command he had received
The priests invented the command themselves
The command applied to only one day
questions.explanation: Moses explains that these instructions came from a command he had received.

paragraphs.title: Aaron and His Sons Obey the Command

easy.question: Who did everything they were commanded to do?
answers: Aaron and his sons
Moses and his sons
The Israelites
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Aaron and his sons did all things.”

easy.question: What did Aaron and his sons do?
answers: They built an altar
They did everything they were commanded
They left the tabernacle
easy.explanation: They did everything the Lord had commanded.

easy.question: Who gave the commands?
answers: Aaron
His sons
The Lord
easy.explanation: The verse says these were the things the Lord commanded.

medium.question: What can we learn from the words “all things”?
answers: They obeyed the command completely
They chose only part of the command
They did not know what to do
medium.explanation: The word “all” shows that Aaron and his sons fulfilled the entire command.

medium.question: In the phrase “which the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses,” what does “by the hand of Moses” mean?
answers: Through Moses
Beside Moses’ hand
Against Moses
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the Lord delivered the command through Moses.

medium.question: What is the order of events in the verse?
answers: Aaron and his sons acted, and afterward the Lord commanded
The Lord commanded through Moses, and Aaron and his sons acted
The Israelites commanded, and Moses acted
medium.explanation: The Lord gave the command through Moses, and Aaron and his sons carried it out.

challenge.question: What quality of Aaron and his sons is emphasized?
answers: Exact obedience to the command
A desire to change the command
Avoiding action
challenge.explanation: The words “all things” emphasize complete and careful obedience.

challenge.question: Why is Moses mentioned at the end of the verse?
answers: To say that he did the work instead of Aaron
To show that he conveyed the Lord’s command to Aaron and his sons
To show that he opposed their service
challenge.explanation: “By the hand of Moses” identifies Moses as the one through whom the command was delivered.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the plural wording “Aaron and his sons”?
answers: Only Aaron was responsible
The sons acted without Aaron
Aaron and his sons participated together in obeying the command
challenge.explanation: The verse names Aaron and his sons together, showing that they shared in carrying out the command.

answers: Exact obedience to the command
A desire to change the command
Avoiding action
questions.explanation: The words “all things” emphasize complete and careful obedience.

answers: To say that he did the work instead of Aaron
To show that he conveyed the Lord’s command to Aaron and his sons
To show that he opposed their service
questions.explanation: “By the hand of Moses” identifies Moses as the one through whom the command was delivered.

answers: Only Aaron was responsible

Aaron and his sons participated together in obeying the command
questions.explanation: The verse names Aaron and his sons together, showing that they shared in carrying out the command.
